security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown formatting false positives, but two ranges contain actual git and python command examples. The network finding is confirmed because the install step clones an external GitHub repository, and a semantic supply-chain concern exists because that URL points outside the audited skill source. No prompt-injection language or data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Ensure the cloned repository matches the audited marketplace source, or document that the external repository is separately reviewed before use.
Add clear review and confirmation steps before running python3 agent-manager scripts or assigning tasks to agents.
Document sandboxing, allowed agent actions, log locations, and cron failure handling for recurring work.

content.value_statement: Coordinating several local agents is hard when sessions, logs, and assignments spread across tools. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a tmux-based workflow for starting, monitoring, and assigning local agents.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup by cloning the agent-manager-skill repository.
Shows commands to run the doctor check and list configured agents.
Shows how to start a named agent in a tmux-managed session.
Shows how to monitor an agent with follow mode.
Shows how to assign a task to an agent with a heredoc prompt.
limitations: Requires tmux and python3 on the local machine.
Depends on scripts and example agent configuration from the referenced repository.
Does not include policy controls for what assigned agents may run.
Does not document authentication, log retention, or sandbox controls.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Local Maintenance Agents
use_cases.description: Start named agents, monitor their sessions, and assign routine maintenance workflows from one command pattern.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Repository Tasks
use_cases.description: Use separate tmux sessions so multiple CLI agents can work on distinct repository tasks at the same time.

use_cases.title: Schedule Recurring Agent Checks
use_cases.description: Plan cron-friendly agent runs for repeated checks, then review output through the monitoring workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-manager-skill to run the doctor check and summarize missing prerequisites before starting agents.

prompt_templates.title: List and Start an Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-manager-skill to list configured agents, start EMP_0001, and report the session status.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor and Assign Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-manager-skill to monitor EMP_0001, assign EMP_0002 a maintenance workflow, and summarize output changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cron Agent Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-manager-skill to design a cron-friendly schedule for three local agents, including monitoring checkpoints and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Check whether my local agent setup is ready.
output_examples.output: A readiness report listing installed prerequisites, configured agents, missing files, and the next safe command to run.

output_examples.input: Start EMP_0001 and monitor its work.
output_examples.output: A concise status update showing the agent session state, recent output, and any errors that need attention.
A task assignment summary with the selected agent, the workflow name, and the monitoring step to verify progress.

best_practices: Run the doctor check before starting agents.
Review the cloned repository and agent definitions before assigning work.
Use named agents and concise task prompts so logs remain traceable.
anti_patterns: Do not run agent commands from an unreviewed repository.
Do not assign broad tasks that allow unrestricted file or network access.
Do not schedule recurring work without log review and failure alerts.

faq.question: Does this skill create the agents?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands for managing agents that are configured under an agents directory.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The skill requires tmux and python3 on the local machine.

faq.question: Can it run multiple agents at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed around separate tmux sessions for parallel local CLI agents.

faq.question: Does it support recurring work?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes cron-friendly scheduling, but the user must configure safe schedules.

faq.question: Is the referenced repository included in this audit?
faq.answer: No. The audit reviewed the skill file, not the external repository cloned by the install command.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
